draft:
Our claim to apostolic practice rests on a story, and our written record shows the practices only from the point where the sources begin [[syr.dw.apostolic]] [[as:paraphrase]].

Addai the apostle came to Edessa, healed the king, and set the church's life in order, and we cherish that story as our legend [[syr.dw.apostolic]] [[syr.story.abgar-addai-legend]] [[as:paraphrase]].

The legend was written down late, and it is not a document from the beginning [[syr.dw.apostolic]] [[as:paraphrase]].

We tell the king's letter to Jesus as our legend, not as our history [[syr.dw.corpus-and-its-edges]] [[as:paraphrase]].

When the sources begin, the practices are already there: assembly on the first day, fasting, the covenant, and the one Gospel as the standard [[syr.dw.apostolic]] [[as:paraphrase]].

Aphrahat's Demonstration 6 attests the covenant, men and women vowed to lifelong celibacy and service inside the town congregation [[syr.gravity.covenant-life]] [[as:paraphrase]].

Our oldest dated word is a line about a flood in Edessa, though we cannot be sure the line stood in the first record and was not added later [[syr.dw.corpus-and-its-edges]] [[as:paraphrase]].

The Chronicle of Edessa, in its entry for the year 513 of the Greeks, records: [[quote:syr.quote.chronicle-flood-line]]

The Addai legend was written down late, and the Addai legend is not a document from the beginning. We tell the king's letter to Jesus as our legend, not as our history. When the sources begin, the practices are already there: assembly on the first day, fasting, the covenant, and the one Gospel as the standard. Aphrahat's Demonstration 6 attests the covenant, men and women vowed to lifelong celibacy and service inside the town congregation. Our oldest dated word is a line about a flood in Edessa, though we cannot be sure the flood line stood in the first record and was not added later.

judgement.reason: It shows only that a church building existed by the flood year and says nothing of rituals, and the record forbids using it as evidence of what Christians did inside the building.

question: What evidence connects your rituals to the earliest followers, rather than later invention?
